title: American Legion Post 59 Receives Wheelchair-Accessible Van to Help Veterans Get to Appointments
excerpt: American Legion Post 59 in Laredo received a donated wheelchair-accessible van, a 2023 Chrysler with a hydraulic lift and room for two wheelchairs, that the post will use to give veterans rides to VA medical appointments, events and celebrations, according to the Laredo Morning Times.
content:
American Legion Post 59 in Laredo has received a donated wheelchair-accessible van that will let the post give rides to veterans who have trouble getting around, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The van, a 2023 Chrysler, was donated by Albert Lowry, a trustee of Post 59. It has a hydraulic lift and room for two wheelchairs, the newspaper reported.

Lowry said his mother-in-law, Diana Benavides Solis, bought the van a year before she gave it to him, and that she enjoyed outings with it. He said he hopes it now serves many veterans.

The post will use the van to take veterans to VA medical appointments, events and celebrations, according to the newspaper. Post Commander Jose M. Gamez Jr. told Lowry that he and other veterans appreciated the donation, saying they will now be able to take care of veterans who cannot get around, and expressing hope the gift encourages others to donate items or support the organization.

The American Legion Arturo T. Benavides Memorial Post 59 was formally established in 2012. Its goal is to support veterans and their families and keep the spirit of service alive, the newspaper reported. The post is named after Benavides, a former post commander who died in 2010, and offers assistance programs, community service, leadership development, scholarships and ceremonies. It is open to eligible veterans and supporters.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 14, 2026.
